title: Edit V-Ray Render Properties
content: ### **Objective** Configure render properties for the final render image. ### **Location** Render Toolbar ▶ ![render_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36781019890457) Render Properties. ### **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu in Location. → Render properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Refer to the below table and edit the settings as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Render Engine** | **Render Engine** | Choose the computer engine to run the render. **CPU** | Run the render with CPU. **GPU (CUDA)** | Run the render with GPU (CUDA). **GPU (OpenCL)** | Run the render with GPU (OpenCL). **CPU Supporting** | Use CPU along with GPU when rendering. Toggle off this option to not use CPU. **📝****Note:** This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as GPU (CUDA). **Low GPU Priority** | Lower GPU priority when rendering. GPU is firstly used in other functions and then used in render. **📝****Note:** This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as either GPU (CUDA) or GPU (OpenCL). **Finish Conditions** | **Noise Threshold** | Set the Noise Threshold for the final render image. The default value is 0.050 and the range is between 0.001 and 0.100. The higher the Noise Threshold is, the more the noise is in the final render image. **Max, Render Time (min)** | The time used for rendering is about two minutes on average when default settings are used for render, light, and image/video properties. However, any modification on the properties may alter the render time. With this option, decide the maximum time that can be used for rendering per image. **Quality** | Adjust the render quality of lights and materials. The Quality can be adjusted to four levels: Low, Medium, High, and Very High. As the option is set towards Very High, render speed decreases. **📝****Note:** * Increase the Quality to render white fur. * Increase the Quality to express light reflections more realistically when textures are added to the studio environment such as the wall and floor. **Light** | Adjust the quality of the light. **Material** | Adjust the quality of materials. **Mesh Optimization** **(Final** **Render Only)** **** **** | **Knitwear** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40170473107609) Optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image. This option only appears when Camera Lens is selected as Default. **Frustum Culling** | No knitwear mesh is created outside the view frustum. A minor difference may appear in the final rendered image when Frustum Culling is enabled. This setting removes all meshes that are out of the camera's view. **LOD** | Level of Detail. The number of knitwear meshes is reduced based on their distance from the camera, with greater distances resulting in fewer meshes. **Color Mapping** | Calibrate the final image color. **Type** **(ver 7.2**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142311561881)**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=LlQ6koe3LMps8Meq&t=3057)**)** | Choose the type of Color Mapping. **Reinhard** | The closer the Burn value is to 1.0, the more the image color is multiplied simply by the brightness, and the closer it is to 0.0, the more the color is saturated by the brightness. **HSV exponential****** | Similar to Reinhard's Burn value of 0.0, the ratio of color (RGB) remains. **📝****Note:** * Use the **Open** , **Save** buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the setting. * To optimize the render speed, please refer to the below directions. 1\. When your OS is Windows: a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select **GPU (CUDA)** for **Engine** for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select **GPU (OpenCL)** for **Engine** for faster render time. 2\. When your OS is Mac:**( ver 2025.0**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142311561881)**](https://youtu.be/UI7jhqvsXdk?si=2K-0IJSklHU3Xw4c)[**)**](https://youtu.be/UI7jhqvsXdk?si=2K-0IJSklHU3Xw4c) a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select **GPU (CUDA)** for **Engine** for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select **CPU** for **Engine** for faster render time.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for configuring render properties to optimize the final render image quality and performance.

title: Edit Texture
content: **List of Contents** Move Zoom In/Out and Rotate Rotate Grainline Setting options **Objective** Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶ **Edit Texture** 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ ![_______2D___.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005711127) **Edit Texture** **Operation** **Move** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click ▶ Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. **Zoom In/Out and Rotate** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a pattern with fabric applied. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. Click on the diagonal, vertical, horizontal lines of the gizmo ▶ drag, or drag along the gizmo circle. → Diagonal line : The size of the texture image is adjusted while the aspect ratio is maintained. → Horizontal/ Vertical: Texture images are scaled only in the vertical and horizontal directions. → Circle : The texture image is rotated. 4. Or select a Fabric and enter the image's [Width and Height](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011527274-Edit-Texture-Size-Property-Editor-) value in Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Texture** Transformation. **※ Note:** * Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. * Edit back of texture when you change **Garment Rendering Style** as [Back Texture Surface.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011148874-2D-Window-Display-Icons-ver5-0-0-and-Above-) **Rotate Grainline** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. → Drag the grainline in the direction you want to rotate it. 4. Simulate once it is adjusted. → The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. **※ Note:** You can directly enter the angle in the Pattern Properties ▶ Fabric ▶ Grain Direction menu, and if you turn off the Link All Colorways menu, you can apply the different grain direction for each colorway. **Setting options** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the pattern and set options as needed. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Assign to New Fabric** | Apply new fabric to selected pattern. **Reset to Basic Fabric** | Reset the fabric of the selected pattern to the properties of the basic fabric. **Reset Fabric Angle** | Resets the texture angle to the original angle. **Align Grain** | Aligns the grainline at an angle parallel to the X, Y, or custom axis. **Match up Grain (ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142221677209)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=TlrDBg3s9NYN3N0U&t=3707)**)** | Align the grainline so that the texture between the selected segment and the baseline continues smoothly. For symmetrical patterns, the selected segment and symmetric line are matched. **Delete Texture** | Delete the texture. **Flip Texture Horizontally/ Vertically** | Flip the texture horizontally or vertically. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for modifying fabric grainlines and adjusting texture images for patterns in a design software, detailing tools and operations for effective texture editing.

Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curve Point** or **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670828/________.png) **Edit Curve Point** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005619007/_______.png)**Edit Pattern** 2. title: How to Create Bézier Curves
content: Create curves in CLO similarly to how they are drawn in Adobe Illustrator. Bézier curves are curves that are controlled and shaped by editing the handles that come with them. The resulting curves are CLO-internal. **※Note:** If a DXF is exported from CLO, Bézier curves are automatically converted to curves made out of Curve Points, a more common-across-software type of curve creation and control. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** or **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005618447/________.png) **Polygon** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670248/__________.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** ** Operation** **How to Create Bézier Curves** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** or **Internal Polygon/Line** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005618447/________.png) **Polygon** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670248/__________.png) **Internal Polygon/Line** 2. Click and drag on the 2D window. The curve is created as the blue handles appear. → Continue to drag to adjust curvature. When the desired curvature is achieved, release your mouse button. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670268/__.png) 3. To draw a straight line or change the direction of the curve, click on the point created last. Then, continue to draw a shape with either the **Polygon** tool or a shape or line with **Internal Polygon/Line** tool. **How to Cancel/Reverse in-between** 1. To cancel all actions, hit the **Esc** key or **Ctrl+Z (Windows) / Cmmd+Z (Mac)** keys on the keyboard. → All the actions taken to create a shape with either the **Polygon** tool or a shape or line with the**Internal Polygon/Line** tool are undone. 2. To cancel the last step, hit the **Delete** or **Backspace** keys on the keyboard. → The point created last is undone.
content_description: Learn how to create and manipulate Bézier curves in CLO, similar to Adobe Illustrator, by using the Polygon and Internal Polygon/Line tools for precise 2D pattern design.

title: Linked Editing
content: **List of Contents** **Setting** **Edit** **Options and Properties** ### **Objective ** You can quickly edit multiple patterns together by linking different pattern outlines. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0?si=dXtDJ8L1wlCfykgp&start=848 ### **Operation** **Setting** 1. Click the 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern (Z) tool. 2. Click one of the two segments to be edited simultaneously, or select multiple segments simultaneously while holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, and Right-click ▶ Link Lines menu. 3. Move the mouse cursor to click the opposite segment you want to edit simultaneously, or hold down the Shift key on your keyboard and click multiple segments. → Linked editing is set to both selected segments. **※ Note :** If the pattern has already been sewn, you can connect it more easily by right-clicking on the sewing line with the 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing(B) tool ▶ clicking the Link Lines menu. Even if it is not sewing, we recommend sewing first and setting Link Lines if necessary. **Edit** 1. Edit one side of the segment set for linked editing with 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern (Z) tool. → Based on the edited segment, the opposite segment is edited in the same direction in a symmetrical direction. **Options and Properties** 1. Click the 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Link tool. 2. Right-click on the segment set for linking and apply options as needed. **Unlink** | Remove the linked editing. ---|--- **Flip Direction** | Set to be simultaneously edited in the same direction. **※ Note:** You can also apply it in the property editor by clicking on the linked editing segment. **Add Sewing to Linking** | If there is no sewing line, a sewing line is added based on both lines set for linked editing.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for efficiently linking and editing multiple pattern segments simultaneously in your design software.

title: Improve Garment Completeness
content: **List of Contents** Apply Fabric Use Hi-Res Garment Tool **Apply Fabric ** \- Use appropriate fabric to check fit correctly. \- Click and drag the desired Fabric file to the Pattern from the Library window. \- Activate the **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png)****Simulate** tool to confirm the change in the 3D Garment’s silhouette. **Use Hi-Res Garment Tool ** \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026895768/mceclip4.png) **Hi-Res Garment** tool to simply improve the Garment completeness. Use this tool to decrease the **Particle Distance** , **Add’l"l Thickness – Collision** , and **Skin Offset** values at once. \- Change the **Simulation Quality to Complete – Nonlinear** to accurately calculate and emulate fabric properties. \- Click **OK** to apply the changes to the 3D Garment. \- Once these settings are applied, depending on the computer specification, Simulation may seem slowed down. Thus, fine-tuning Garments at this stage is not recommended. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on applying fabrics and utilizing the Hi-Res Garment Tool to enhance the fit and quality of 3D garments in design software.

title: Brief Draping Procedure in CLO
content: **List of Contents** Import DXF file Duplicate Half Patterns Arrangement Sewing Simulation **Import DXF file ** \- To create and drape a 3D Garment, please load Patterns created in a 2D CAD program. \- Double click the folder with practice files that you added to the Library window and double click the DXF file to open. When a pop-up window appears, click OK. **Duplicate Half Patterns ** \- When there are only half Patterns, you must duplicate to create other halves. \- Select all Patterns and right click to access the right-click pop-up menu. Select the **Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)** menu from the pop-up menu. When Patterns are duplicated with above options, any Pattern modification and added Sewing Lines are automatically reflected to symmetric Patterns. **Arrangement ** \- Use the Arrangement Points to place Patterns around an Avatar. \- When symmetric Patterns are placed on symmetric Arrangement Points, their pairs are arranged automatically on the symmetric Arrangement Points. **Sewing ** \- Use the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool interchangeably to establish Sewing Lines. \- When there is no points on the segment to be sewn, use the Segment Sewing tool. However, when there are points on the segment to be sewn, use the Free Sewing tool. \- Please check twisted parts of Sewing Lines while establishing them. **Simulation ** \- Select the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024318527/mceclip3.png) **Simulate** tool to complete the Garment as Patterns fall and drape on the Avatar. Closer the Patterns are placed around the Avatar, faster the Simulation is. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing DXF files, duplicating patterns, arranging them around an avatar, establishing sewing lines, and simulating garment draping in a 3D design environment.

title: Arrangement
content: \- For faster and easier Simulation, arrange Patterns around an Avatar. \- You may click and drag to arrange Patterns in the 3D window, but use Arrangement Points for faster work. Hover the mouse over the second icon in the Vertical Toggle Menu in the 3D window and select **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)****Show Arrangement Points** icon. \- When using the Arrangement Points, select the Pattern to be placed and then click the desired Arrangement Point. \- When Patterns are arranged with the Arrangement Point, it is placed in curve around an Avatar. To turn off the Arrangement Points, select the Show Arrangement Points icon again. \- You may click and drag to move Patterns even after placing them using the Arrangement Points.
content_description: Optimize your 3D simulation experience by efficiently arranging patterns around an avatar using Arrangement Points for quick placement and easy adjustments.

title: Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Sewing Segment Sewing Free Sewing **Sewing** \- To join Patterns, they have to be connected with Sewing Lines. \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** or the >![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar to establish Sewing Lines on Patterns. **Segment Sewing ** \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png)**Segment Sewing** tool to sew segments between two points. \- Click each segments to be sewn to establish a pair of Sewing Lines. \- When establishing the Sewing Lines, be mindful of Directional Notches as they should not be twisted. \- After creating the Sewing Lines between Patterns, Patterns are joined in the 3D window when Simulated. **Free Sewing ** \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool freely establish Sewing Lines along Pattern outlines and Internal Lines, arbitrary deciding start and end points of the Sewing Lines. \- Click four times in total to create a pair of Free Sewing Lines. Click on a Pattern outline or an Internal Line to create a start point and drag the mouse to decide the direction of the Sewing Line. Then, click again to complete the first half of the Sewing Line. Then, create the other half of the Sewing Line on Pattern outline or Internal Line which the first half of the Sewing Line is to be attached to. \- Be mindful to not twist Directional Notches when using the Free Sewing tool as well. \- When the Simulation is activated after creating Sewing Lines, sewn Patterns are joined in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide on using Segment and Free Sewing tools in Clo3D to effectively establish Sewing Lines on patterns for 3D garment simulation.

title: Simulation
content: \- Use the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024318527/mceclip3.png) **Simulate** tool to apply gravity to the 3D window. \- When the Simulate tool is selected from the 3D toobar, all unfixed Patterns fall down to the ground as gravity is applied to the 3D window. \- If you click and drag Patterns while the Simulation is activated, they move like real fabrics. \- However, if you click and drag Patterns while the Simulation is deactivated, they move rigidly as a whole as gravity is no longer applied to the 3D window.
content_description: Explore how to utilize the Simulate tool to apply realistic gravity effects to your 3D patterns, allowing for dynamic movement like real fabrics in your designs.

title: View Control – 2D
content: \- Roll up and down the mouse cursor wheel to zoom out and in the 2D window respectively. \- Hold down the mouse cursor wheel and drag to pan the 2D window.
content_description: This web page provides intuitive controls for zooming and panning a 2D window using the mouse cursor wheel.

title: View Control – 3D
content: **List of Contents** Zoom In/ Zoom Out 3D Window Pan 3D Window Rotate 3D Window View Control Menus **Zoom In/ Zoom Out 3D Window** **** \- Roll up and down the mouse cursor wheel to zoom out and in the 3D window respectively. **Pan 3D Window** \- Hold down the mouse cursor wheel and drag to pan the 3D window. **Rotate 3D Window ** \- Hold down and drag the right button on the mouse to rotate the 3D window in 360° and view every nook and corner of the 3D Garment. **View Control Menus** \- Use the menus related to view control to see front, back and more sides of the Avatar in the 3D window. \- You may access the menus in the right-click pop-up menu. Right click an empty place in the 3D window to access the right-click pop-up and choose Front, Back, Left, Right and more as needed. \- Memorize the shortcuts next to each menu for more efficient work. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to effectively navigate and control the 3D window features, including zooming, panning, rotating, and utilizing view control menus for an enhanced interactive experience.

title: Windows
content: **List of Contents** Library 3D Window / 2D Window / Object Browser / Property Editor Buttons at the Bottom **Library** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJN1eh-bnpE \- The Library window is located on the furthest left. \- Open and use default assets provided by CLO such as Avatar, Garment, Trim, and more. Add frequently used folders to the Library window and access directly in CLO. \- To add a frequently used folder to the Library window, select the Add button and choose the folder to be added from the File Browser. Then, click Select Folder. \- Add the Quickstart_Files folder which contains Quick Start exercise files. \- **Download exercise files[here](https://s3.amazonaws.com/CLOdata/CLO3D_Training/CLO3DCOM+Online+Lessons/Lesson_041718.zip).** **3D Window / 2D Window / Object Browser / Property Editor** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=neOOgRsIFeU \- The 3D window is on the Library window’s right. In the 3D window, you may load Avatar and Dummy to drape and move 3D Garments. \- The 2D window is on the 3D window’s right. Load DXF files to edit and sew Patterns. \- In the Object Browser, you may see all items in the 3D and 2D windows. The Fabric tab is selected by default. \- Properties related to the selected item from the Object Browser appear in the Property Editor. Check and edit properties. **Buttons at the Bottom ** \- You may find three buttons at the right bottom corner of the software. \- Click the button in the middle to hide the 2D window and only show the 3D window. Click the button on the right to hide the 3D window and only show the 2D window. To see both 3D and 2D windows, click the button on the left. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to the CLO software interface, detailing the functionality of the Library, 3D and 2D windows, Object Browser, Property Editor, and navigation buttons for an enhanced user experience.

title: Adjusting a Shirt
content: **List of Contents** Loading an Avatar Importing a DXF file Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window Sewing Patterns Expressing Sleeve Plackets Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window Adding Buttons Simulation Using the Fold Arrangement Tool to Fold the Collar Simulation Changing the Avatar Pose **[Download exercise file](https://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/B_Basic/B-b_Adjusting%20a%20Shirt.zip) for Adjusting a Shirt** **Loading an Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fq_hcHboRXs \- This is a Women’s shirt. Load a female Avatar from the Library. \- Navigate to and double click on the default folder named Avatar in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatars will appear—double click on or drag and drop either female Avatar into the 3D Window. ** Importing a DXF file** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mIXuVCKSjWk \- Import the file, Shirts_Female.dxf for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to B_Basics, then b_Adjusting a Shirt. Double click on the file, Shirts_Female.dxf, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. \- If the practice folder has not been added to the Library, navigate to File > Import > **DXF (ASTM/AAMA)**. Locate FILENAME and click Open to import the file. Set the units to mm and then click OK to finish importing the shirt. **Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window** * **Arranging Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_RbLHS2DV1A \- Arrange the Patterns around the silhouette of the Avatar in the 2D Window. The layout of the Patterns will be reflected in the 3D Window. \- Select the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191348/mceclip7.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Window. In the 2D grid, click and drag over the cuff and placket Patterns. Make sure that the marquee box fully encompasses the Patterns. Place the selected Patterns next to the sleeve Patterns. \- Similarly, select the collar and collar stand Patterns and place them next to the back body Patterns. * **Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GfeRbtv3-og \- Only half of the Garment Patterns have been provided. Duplicate the front, back, and the sleeve Patterns as Symmetric Patterns to complete the 3D Garment. Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar to select the Patterns. Click on the 2D grid and drag the mouse over all the Patterns so that they are fully encompassed within the marquee box. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. \- Right click on one of the Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Navigate to the section labeled Clone Patterns with Linked Editing. Select Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing). \- A ghost of the copied Patterns will follow the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D grid to Paste. Both the selected Patterns and any Sewing relationships they have will be duplicated. * **Arranging the Cloned Patterns in the 2D Window ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OfRcurPiwZk \- Place the duplicated Patterns near the original Patterns. Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, move the duplicated back Pattern close to the original back Pattern in the 2D Window. * **Reset 2D Arrangement (All) ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y0My785iXBM \- Navigate to the 3D Window and select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190828/mceclip1.png)****Reset 2D Arrangement** tool. The Pattern layout in the 2D Window will be reflected to the 3D Window. **Sewing Patterns** * **Sewing the Front and Back** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4nx7WWVajuc \- Sew the shoulder seams using the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)Segment Sewing** tool. (Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) **Free Sewing** tool to match the notches of seams if they are not split based on notches.) \- Sew the yoke Patterns to the back shirt Patterns. \- Join the shirt front and back Patterns at the side seams. \- To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use the respective **M:N Sewing** tool. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool or the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) Free Sewing** tool to select the respective **M:N Sewing** tool. * **Sewing the Sleeves** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_bl-KgZfO4 \- Be mindful of the 2D CAD notches while sewing sleeve caps to their respective armholes. \- Use the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** tool to match the notches of seams if the Pattern outlines are not split based on notches. When the Pattern outlines are split based on their 2D CAD notches, use the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool. \- To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use the respective **M:N Sewing** tool. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool or the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** tool to select the respective **M:N Sewing** tool. \- Use the **M:N Sewing** , **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** or **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tools interchangeably as needed. \- Be mindful of the Directional Notches while Sewing so as not to twist any Sewing Lines. * **Sewing the Collar Pattern to the Body** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BbX5CtxCJyA \- Use either the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png)M:N Free Sewing** or **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png)M:N Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew the collar to the body of the shirt. \- Start sewing from Center Back. To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use the respective **M:N Sewing** tool. To do so, navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool or the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** tool to select the respective **M:N Sewing** tool. \- Use the M:N Sewing,**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) Free Sewing** or **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tools interchangeably as needed. * **Sewing Center Back Seams ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XiwyDDELEdA \- Sew the Center Back seams of the collar, back yoke and back body Patterns to their respective pairs to maintain their Symmetric link. \- The Patterns will be Merged at Center Back later in the tutorial. **Expressing Sleeve Plackets** * **Expressing Sleeve Openings** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nCJWzHeqkNg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112267/mceclip2.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the purple Baseline that will be used to express the sleeve opening. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard. \- Right click on the newly created Internal Line to access a pop-up menu. Select Cut and the sleeve Pattern will be Cut based on the selected Internal Line.。 \- Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191348/mceclip7.png) **Edit Pattern** tool to edit the length of the sleeve opening. Click and drag the vertex of the Cut line to adjust its length. * **Creating Internal Lines to Sew Placket Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3dy5Wjc3QZs \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112267/mceclip2.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the purple Baselines marking where the placket Patterns will be sewn to. \- Hold down the Shift key from the keyboard to select segmented Baselines. Hit the Enter key to Trace them as a single connected Internal Line. \- Hover the mouse over the placket Pattern. Select and trace Baselines on the placket Pattern that indicate where the sleeve Patterns will be sewn to. * **Sewing Placket Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ucqJ5lic-Kg3 \- Use the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) Free Sewing** tool to sew the placket Patterns to the sleeve Patterns. \- When establishing Sewing Lines, be mindful of the side of the placket that needs to remain open. Do not sew that portion of the sleeve to the placket. * **Sewing Cuffs to Sleeves** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-i9h7hqWei8 \- Use the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png)****M:N Free Sewing** tool to sew the cuffs to the sleeves. \- Establish Sewing Lines on the cuff Patterns, starting from the right and moving towards the left. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete the first half of the seam. \- To establish the second half of the seam, start creating Sewing Lines on the placket Patterns and continue onto the sleeve Patterns. Do not sew the Tucks as they will be folded. Be mindful of the Directional Notches while Sewing so as not to twist any Sewing Lines. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete the seam. * **Assigning Fold Angles to Tucks ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e9xcYgL-crc \- Assign Fold Angles to the Tuck so that it folds during Simulation. \- Create Internal Lines by using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112267/mceclip2.png) **Trace** tool. Select the two purple Baselines that are the furthest away from the placket. Fold Angles will be assigned to them. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard. Change the Fold Angle for the Internal Line furthest from the placket. Select it with the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191348/mceclip7.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, navigate to the Property Editor, and changing the Fold Angle to 0. Change the Fold Angle to 360 for the other Internal Line. * **Sewing Tucks ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mgq4MyETTrY \- Sew the Tucks. Make sure their Directional Notches face each other.。 \- Use the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** tool or the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool as needed. \- When the Sewing Lines have all been established, change to the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191348/mceclip7.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. Select the Sewing Lines on the Tucks and navigate to the Property Editor. Change the Sewing Line type to Turned. Now the Tucks will lay flat when Simulation is activated. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window** * **Turning on Arrangement Points** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYBOHPhy068 \- Hover over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png) Avatar Display** icon—the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu—to access elements of the Avatar that can be toggled on or off. Click on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)Show Arrangement Points** , which is the second icon in the horizontal Avatar Display series. Blue dots, the Arrangement Points, will appear on the Avatar in the 3D Window. * **Accessing Arrangement Points Hidden by Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6kjhlZ6kVlI \- Move Patterns that are hiding the Arrangement Points for easier access. \- Hold down Ctrl or Cmd + A to select all Patterns. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. With the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png)****Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar selected, click and drag the Patterns out of the way of the Arrangement Points. * **Preparing Patterns for Easy Arrangement ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u-cwZj1nLCA \- When two Patterns or more are placed together on a single Arrangement Point, the distance between the Patterns will be reflected in the 3D Arrangement. It is best to place patterns close to each other before before placing them on Arrangement Points. \- With the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png)****Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar selected, place Patterns that will be sewn together in close proximity. \- For the shirt front Patterns, place the right front Pattern above the left front Pattern, overlapping slightly at Center Front. \- To do so, use the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png)****Select/Move** tool and select the right shirt front Pattern to access the Gizmo tool. Pull the Pattern slightly forward, away from the left shirt front Pattern to avoid Simulation instability. * **Arranging the Body and Sleeve Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FoAdUwcaY38 \- Select the Pattern first and then the Arrangement Point. The Pattern will curve around the body when placed. Select both front Patterns and place them on an Arrangement Point at Center Front. Repeat for the back Patterns. \- Select both the placket and sleeve Patterns and choose the Arrangement Point located on the bicep. In this particular file, the Arrangement Points on the Avatar’s arms are linked. This means that when a Symmetric sleeve Pattern is placed on an Arrangement Point on one arm, the other sleeve will arrange itself similarly on the other arm. \- All Arrangement Points, except for those that are placed around the torso of the Avatar, are linked in CLO Enterprise v.3.0. Symmetrized Arrangement Points have a light blue outline around them. \- Make sure to place the placket Patterns slightly above the sleeve Patterns in the 3D Window before arranging them together on the Arrangement Point. * **Arranging Collar Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6SfnfmPs1GY \- Place collar Patterns on the Arrangement Point on the back neck of the Avatar. **Adding Buttons** * **Adding Buttonholes** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sb1eJcWL1Uo \- Add Buttonholes to the wearer’s right front shirt Pattern. \- Select the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024193968/mceclip4.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window. There are purple Chalk Lines on the Pattern to indicate Buttonhole placement. Click once on the Pattern to add a Buttonhole. A line, representing the Buttonhole, will appear on the 2D Pattern and an image of the Buttonhole will appear in the 3D. \- Select the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024193988/mceclip5.png) **Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. In the 2D Window, click on the newly created Buttonhole to select it. Hold down the Ctrl or Cmd + C keys on the keyboard to Copy and then hold down the Ctrl or Cmd + V keys to Paste. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to move the Buttonhole in vertical straight line. Hover the mouse over the second Baseline marking the Buttonhole and right click to access the Paste pop-up window. Enter the number of Buttonholes and their Offset distance. Click OK to generate the Buttonholes. * **Adding Buttons** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DsTvFpJuoQU \- Add Buttons to the wearer’s left front shirt Pattern. \- Select the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024113627/mceclip6.png) **Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window. There are purple Chalk Lines on the Pattern to indicate Button placement. Click once on the Pattern to add a Button. A circle with a cross in the middle, representing the Button, will appear on the 2D Pattern and a Button will appear in the 3D. \- Select the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024193988/mceclip5.png) **Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. In the 2D Window, click on the newly created Button to select it. Hold down the Ctrl or Cmd + C keys on the keyboard to Copy and then hold down the Ctrl or Cmd + V keys to Paste. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to move the Buttonhole in vertical straight line. Hover the mouse over the second Baseline marking the Button and right click to access the Paste pop-up window. Enter the number of Buttons and their Offset distance. Click OK to generate the Buttons. * **Adding Buttons and Buttonholes to the Cuffs and Collar Stand ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=osXwAdSbq00 \- Repeat the same procedure listed in the previous step to add Buttons and Buttonholes to the cuffs and collar stand. \- To rotate the Buttonholes, select the**![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024193988/mceclip5.png) Select/Move Button** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on the Buttonhole to be rotated and navigate to the Property Editor. Enter the desired angle that the Button will be rotated to. * **Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N75t2x3e88k \- Select the ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024194348/mceclip7.png)**Fasten Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click on Buttons and Buttonholes to pair them up in either in the 2D or 3D Window. The selection order does not affect Simulation. \- Buttons will appear on top of the Buttonhole they are paired with. Go to C_Details, then a_Constructing a Collar Lapel. Double click on the file, Jacket_Lapel&collar, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. ** Changing Sewing Line Type** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsMvUAGrgX8 \- There are two types of Sewing Lines: Flat and Turned. \- If overlapping Patterns, in this case the jacket shell and its lining, are sewn with Flat Sewing Lines, there is a higher chance of collision and Simulation instability when they are folded together. To prevent this, change Flat Sewing Lines to Turned Sewing Lines within the Property Editor. \- Select the **Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Click on a Sewing Line and navigate to the Property Editor. Click the drop down arrow next to **Sewing Line Type**. Select **Turned Sewing**. \- The lapels will now lay flat. **Using the Fold Arrangement Tool to Fold the Lapels** * **Tracing a Roll Line ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9o0ztX4nb4k \- The ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png) **Fold Arrangement** tool can only be applied to seamlines and Internal Lines. Thus, Chalk Lines and Baselines must be Traced as Internal Lines in order to fold them. \- The roll line is marked by a purple Baseline on the Pattern. Select the ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239328/mceclip2.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D Toolbar and click on the Baseline. \- When Patterns are Symmetrized/Symmetrically Pasted, the Baseline only needs to be traced on one of the Patterns. If the Patterns are not Symmetrized/Symmetrically Pasted, Trace the Baselines on both Patterns. \- With the Baselines selected, hit the Enter key to Trace them and generate the Internal Lines. * **Folding the Lapels ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M6ZWBb57BKg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png) **Fold Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click on the newly created roll line on the jacket shell and the Fold Arrangement Gizmo will appear. Use the arrows to fold the lapel. Repeat for the roll line on the jacket lining. \- Avoid overlapping the shell and the lining Patterns while folding them. * **Assigning a Fold Angle ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h6cyzqPTTt8 \- To fold lapels more precisely, assign a Fold Angle to the roll lines. \- Select the fold lines on the 2D Patterns with the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239368/mceclip4.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Drag the mouse and double click on Center Back to end the roll line. The Internal Line will be reflected to the other half of the Symmetrically Pasted Patterns. * **Folding the Collar ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DJsnGVukEKw \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239308/mceclip1.png) **Fold Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. Click on the newly created roll line and the Fold Arrangement Gizmo will appear. Use the arrows to fold the collar Pattern. * **Assigning a Fold Angle ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qgsDfr-xUlE \- To fold the collar more precisely, assign a Fold Angle to the roll line. \- Select the roll line on the 2D Patterns with the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024239368/mceclip4.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. Navigate to the Property Editor. Under **Fold** , set the **Fold Angle** to **360** degrees. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S8rIvkBLsRw/span> \- Click on the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to drape. title: Adjusting a Jacket
content: **List of Contents** Loading an Avatar Importing a DXF file Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window Sewing Patterns Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window Adding Buttons and Buttonholes Simulation Changing the Avatar Pose **[Download exercise file](https://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/B_Basic/B-e_Adjusting%20a%20Jacket.zip) for Adjusting a Jacket** **Loading an Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6lw-xnPb_fg \- This is a Women’s jacket. Load a female Avatar from the Library. \- Navigate to and double click on the default folder named Avatar in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatars will appear—double click on or drag and drop either female Avatar into the 3D Window. ** Importing a DXF file** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sYtsv8idu7A \- Import the file, Jacket_female.dxf, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to B_Basics, then e_Adjusting a Jacket. Double click on the file, Jacket_female.dxf, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. \- If the practice folder has not been added to the Library, navigate to File > Import > **DXF (ASTM/AAMA)**. Locate the file, Jacket_female.dxf, and click Open to import the file. Set the units to mm and then click OK to finish importing the jacket. **Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window** * **Arranging Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rEiKY7nEIaM \- Arrange the Patterns around the silhouette of the Avatar in the 2D Window. The layout of the Patterns will be reflected in the 3D Window. \- Select the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153087/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Window. In the 2D grid, click and drag over the sleeve Patterns. Be sure to encompass all the sleeve Patterns within the marquee box to select them properly. Selected sleeve Patterns will be highlighted in yellow. Right click on Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Select **Flip Horizontally**. \- Place the flipped sleeve Patterns in between the Front and Back Patterns for convenience while Sewing. Sleeve caps should face their respective armholes. * **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing) ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vpbveIJR_5Y \- Only half of the Garment Patterns have been provided. Duplicate the front, back, and the sleeve Patterns as Symmetric Patterns to complete the 3D Garment. Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar to select the Patterns. Click on the 2D grid and drag the mouse over all the Patterns so that they are fully encompassed within the marquee box. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. \- Right click on one of the Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Navigate to the section labeled **Clone Patterns with Linked Editing**. Select **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)**. \- A ghost of the copied pattern will follow the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D grid to Paste. Both the selected Patterns and any Sewing relationships they have will be duplicated. * **Arranging the Cloned Patterns in the 2D Window ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JIyR1AOSD2c \- Place the duplicated Patterns near the original Patterns. Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, move the duplicated back Pattern close to the original back Pattern in the 2D Window. **Sewing Patterns** * **Sewing Shoulder Seams ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UbubLJXRGhU \- Since the shoulder seams are split into multiple segments based on their 2D CAD notches, use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool to establish Sewing Lines. (Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to match the notches of seams if they have not been split based on notches previously established in the 2D CAD software the Patterns were exported from.) \- To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use **M:N Sewing**. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to select the respective ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png) **M:N Sewing** tool from the drop down menu. \- Change back to the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool to sew two individual Patterns together. * **Sewing the Front and Back ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k4ssPWg2dM4 \- Sew all the panels for the front of the jacket together. Repeat for the back panel pieces. When completed, sew the jacket front and back together at the side seams. \- Since the front and back Pattern outlines are split into multiple segments based on their 2D CAD notches, use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool to sew. (Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to match the notches of seams if seams are not split based on notches previously established in the 2D CAD software the Patterns were exported from.) \- To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use **M:N Sewing**. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to select the respective ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png) **M:N Sewing** tool from the drop down menu. \- Change back to the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool to sew two individual Patterns together. * **Sewing the Sleeves ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MyCViPqedGg \- Sew the two-piece sleeve together. \- Be mindful of the Pattern notches while sewing the sleeve caps to their respective armholes. \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to match the notches of seams if they are not split based on 2D CAD notches. Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool if Pattern outlines are split into multiple segments based on the notches previously established in the 2D CAD software the Patterns were exported from. \- To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use **M:N Sewing**. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to select the respective ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png) **M:N Sewing** tool from the drop down menu. \- Be mindful of the Directional Notches while Sewing so as not to twist any Sewing Lines. * **Sewing the Collar to the Body ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=liIcm3vtNxU \- Use either the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png) **M:N Free Sewing** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew the collar to the body of the jacket. \- Start the Sewing Line from Center Back. To sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern, use **M:N Sewing**. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024153567/mceclip2.png) **Free Sewing** tool to select the respective ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png) **M:N Sewing** tool from the drop down menu. \- Be mindful of the Directional Notches while sewing so as not to twist any Sewing Lines. \- Change back to the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024234328/mceclip1.png) Segment Sewing** tool to sew two individual Patterns together. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window ** * **Syncing Pattern Arrangement YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZZ9Yy6g2NdM **\- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190828/mceclip1.png)****Reset 2D Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar to reflect the Pattern layout in the 3D Window as it is in the 2D Window. \- The Pattern Arrangement in both the 2D and 3D Windows will appear the same. * **Turning on Arrangement Points ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-Gsj960XVs \- Hover over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png)****Avatar Display** icon—the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu—to access elements of the Avatar that can be toggled on or off. Click on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)****Show Arrangement Points** , which is the second icon in the horizontal Avatar Display series. Blue dots, the Arrangement Points, will appear on the Avatar in the 3D Window. * **Accessing Arrangement Points Hidden by Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RECoku1_IpM \- Move Patterns that are hiding the Arrangement Points for easier access. \- Hold down Ctrl or Cmd + A to select all Patterns. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar selected, click and drag the Patterns out of the way of the Arrangement Points. * **Preparing Patterns for Easy Arrangement YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SeaBlbNdahY **\- For optimal placement of the jacket front panels, place the wearer’s right front Pattern above the wearer’s left front Pattern, with a small overlap at Center Front. \- To do so, using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool, select the wearer’s right front panel in the 3D Window to access the Gizmo tool. The Pattern will curve around the body when placed. Select both front Patterns and place them on an Arrangement Point at Center Front. This means that when a Symmetric sleeve Pattern is placed on an Arrangement Point on one arm, the other sleeve will arrange itself similarly on the other arm. \- All Arrangement Points, except for those that are placed around the torso of the Avatar, are linked in CLO ver4.0.0. Symmetrized Arrangement Points have light-blue outlines around them. * **Arranging the Collar YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VZqGU3Gfobc **\- Place the collar Patterns on the Arrangement Point located at the Avatar’s back neck. **Adding Buttons and Buttonholes** * **Adding Buttonholes ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cRgD9FdQPXo \- Add Buttonholes to the wearer’s right front jacket panel. \- Select the ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024235748/mceclip3.png) **Buttonhole** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the wearer’s right front jacket panel in the 2D Window. There are purple Chalk Lines on the Pattern to indicate Buttonhole placement. Click once on the Pattern to add a Buttonhole. A line, representing the Buttonhole, will appear on the 2D Pattern and an image of the Buttonhole will appear in the 3D. Add Buttonholes to the entire Pattern where indicated. * **Adding Buttons ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dp3-iteohiw \- Add Buttons to the wearer’s left front jacket panel. \- Select the ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024154767/mceclip4.png) **Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the wearer’s left front jacket panel in the 2D Window. There are purple Chalk Lines on the Pattern to indicate Button placement. Click once on the Pattern to add a Button. A circle with a cross in the middle, representing the Button, will appear on the 2D Pattern and a Button will appear in the 3D. Add Buttons to the entire Pattern where indicated. * **Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfYFxALNxo4 \- Select the ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024235768/mceclip5.png) **Fasten Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click on Buttons and Buttonholes to pair them up in either in the 2D or 3D Window. The selection order does not affect Simulation. \- Buttons will appear on top of the Buttonhole they are paired with. The lock icon hovering above the pairs indicate that the Buttons and Buttonholes have been fastened. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1KTT2ZKoHeI \- Click on the**![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to apply the changes. Click **![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png)Simulate** again to turn it off when the 3D Garment is fully draped. **Changing the Avatar Pose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ofKCHrm7uCY \- Change the Avatar Pose from A-pose to have her stand at attention. \- To apply the Pose, navigate to and double click on the default folder named Pose in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatar faces will appear—double click on the folder that matches the Avatar in the 3D Window. Double click on or drag and drop the file pose_02_attention.pos to apply the pose. Using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar, move the duplicated back Pattern close to the original back Pattern in the 2D Window. **Sewing Patterns ** * **Sewing the Front and Back** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YIyS5kkepCM \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png) **Segment Sewing** and**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) Free Sewing** tools interchangeably as needed. \- Sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern using the **M:N Sewing** tool. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar. Click and hold either the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png) **Segment Sewing** tool or the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** tool to select the respective**M:N Sewing** tool. * **Sewing the Sleeve Caps to the Armholes** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VP8OO0pxe04 \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png) **Segment Sewing** and **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png)****Free Sewing** tools interchangeably as needed. \- Be mindful of the Directional Notches while sewing so as not to twist any Sewing Lines. * **Sewing the Collar Pattern to the Neckline ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mcXTsCGTnD8 \- Use either the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png) M:N Free Sewing** or **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png)****M:N Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew the collar to the body of the jumper. * **Sewing Zippers** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QE35fBMKSk8 \- In CLO, users need to generate zipper Patterns to express zippers. Utilize either **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024192788/mceclip0.png)****M:N Free Sewing** or**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024112247/mceclip1.png) M:N Segment Sewing** from the 2D Toolbar to sew the zipper to the body and neck Patterns. Sew the zipper Patterns together to fasten the jumper shut. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window** * **Syncing Pattern Arrangement** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h9bAczVFsUQ \- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190828/mceclip1.png)****Reset 2D Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar to reflect the Pattern layout in the 3D Window as it is in the 2D Window. \- The Pattern Arrangement in both the 2D and 3D Windows will appear the same. * **Turning on Arrangement Points** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oGxryxxPgYQ \- Hover over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png)****Avatar Display** icon—the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu—to access elements of the Avatar that can be toggled on or off. Click on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)****Show Arrangement Points** , which is the second icon in the horizontal Avatar Display series. Blue dots, the Arrangement Points, will appear on the Avatar in the 3D Window. * **Accessing Arrangement Points Hidden by Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yDXkFS1aRfY \- Move Patterns that are hiding the Arrangement Points for easier access. \- Hold down Ctrl or Cmd +A to select all Patterns. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. With the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png)****Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar selected, click and drag the Patterns out of the way of the Arrangement Points. * **Arranging the Body and Sleeve Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1C1gEQH7P_g \- Select the Pattern first and then the Arrangement Point. The Pattern will curve around the body when placed. Select both front Patterns and place them on an Arrangement Point at Center Front. Repeat for the back Patterns. \- For the sleeves, choose the Arrangement Point located on the bicep. In this particular file, the Arrangement Points on the Avatar’s arms are linked. This means that when a Symmetric sleeve Pattern is placed on an Arrangement Point on one arm, the other sleeve will arrange itself similarly on the other arm. \- All Arrangement Points, except for those that are placed around the torso of the Avatar, are linked in CLO ver4.0.0. Symmetrized Arrangement Points have light-blue outlines around them. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P8tGej4VJ5A \- Click on the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) Simulate icon in the 3D Toolbar to apply the changes. Click ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) Simulate again to turn it off when the 3D Garment is fully draped. **Changing the Avatar Pose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u_Trf2aqgu8 \- Change the Avatar Pose from A-pose to have him stand at attention. \- To apply the Pose, navigate to and double click on the default folder named Pose in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatar faces will appear—double click on the folder that matches the Avatar in the 3D Window. Double click on or drag and drop the file pose_02_attention.pos to apply the pose. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Adjusting Pants
content: **List of Contents** Loading an Avatar Importing a DXF file Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window Sewing Patterns Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window Sewing the Waistband Applying Bonding Simulation Changing the Avatar Pose **[Download exercise file](https://clo3d.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/web/zendesk/B_Basic/B-d_Adjusting%20Pants.zip) for Adjusting Pants** **Loading an Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38XWMgxRU4w \- This is a Women’s pant. Load a female Avatar from the Library. \- Navigate to and double click on the default folder named Avatar in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatars will appear—double click on or drag and drop either female Avatar into the 3D Window. ** ****Importing a DXF file** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fryiRWJx70k \- Import the file, Pants_Female.dxf, for this exercise. (Download the practice files before starting this tutorial.) \- To do so, navigate to the CLO Tutorial folder, which was previously added in the Introduction to CLO tutorial, within the Library. Go to B_Basics, then d_Adjusting Pants. Double click on the file, Pants_Female.dxf, or drag and drop it into either the 3D or 2D Window. \- If the practice folder has not been added to the Library, navigate to File > Import > **DXF (ASTM/AAMA)**. Locate the file, Pants_Female.dxf, and click Open to import the file. Set the units to mm and then click OK to finish importing the pants. **Arranging Patterns in the 2D Window** * **Arranging Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r-OEEj3t4B4 \- Arrange the Patterns around the silhouette of the Avatar in the 2D Window. The layout of the Patterns will be reflected in the 3D Window. * **Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing) ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v9MuQADcvD8 \- Only half of the Garment Patterns have been provided. Duplicate the front, back, and the sleeve Patterns as Symmetric Patterns to complete the 3D Garment. Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar to select the Patterns. Click on the 2D grid and drag the mouse over all the Patterns so that they are fully encompassed within the marquee box. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. \- Right click on one of the Patterns to access a pop-up menu. Navigate to the section labeled Clone Patterns With Linked Editing. Select **Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)**. \- A ghost of the copied Patterns will follow your mouse cursor. Click on the 2D grid to Paste. Both the selected Patterns and any Sewing relationships they have will be duplicated. **Sewing Patterns** * **Sewing the Pants ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmanuouKfew \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) **Free Sewing** tool to sew the pocket and yoke Patterns to the pant Patterns. \- Establish Sewing Lines where the pocket Patterns overlap with the front pant Patterns. \- Establish Sewing Lines where the yoke connects to the back pant Patterns. * **Sewing the Side Seams, Center Front, and Center Back ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c09omjerHCA -The pant is divided into multiple Patterns. Use the **M:N Sewing** tool from the 2D Toolbar to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern or several other Patterns as needed. \- Change back to the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) **Free Sewing** tool to sew two individual Patterns together. * **Sewing the Waistband to the Pant Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8AsoSnpNlIg \- Attach the waistband Patterns to the pant Patterns. \- Use the **M:N Sewing** tool, the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110887/mceclip4.png) **Free Sewing** tool, or the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191248/mceclip3.png)****Segment Sewing** tool interchangeably as needed. **Arranging Patterns in the 3D Window ** * **Syncing Pattern Arrangement YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3QOz9JCpMAI **\- Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190828/mceclip1.png)****Reset 2D Arrangement** tool from the 3D Toolbar to reflect the Pattern layout in the 3D Window as it is in the 2D Window. \- The Pattern Arrangement in both the 2D and 3D Windows will appear the same. * **Turning on Arrangement Points ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_jbTL8va7g8 \- Hover over the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024189368/mceclip6.png)****Avatar Display** icon—the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu—to access elements of the Avatar that can be toggled on or off. Click on **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024108407/mceclip5.png)****Show Arrangement Points** , which is the second icon in the horizontal Avatar Display series. Blue dots, the Arrangement Points, will appear on the Avatar in the 3D Window. * **Accessing Arrangement Points Hidden by Patterns ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NgyBf3VE7wc \- Move Patterns that are hiding the Arrangement Points for easier access. \- Hold down Ctrl or Cmd + A to select all Patterns. The Patterns will be highlighted in yellow to indicate they have been selected. With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D Toolbar selected, click and drag the Patterns out of the way of the Arrangement Points. * **Arranging the Front Pant Patterns YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGalFvPH6eg **\- The front pant and pocket Patterns need to be arranged together. \- In the 3D Window, place the pocket Patterns underneath the front pant Patterns using the Gizmo tool. To do so, navigate to the 3D Toolbar and choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024110327/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool. Select the front pant and pocket Patterns and click on an Arrangement Point to place them around the Avatar. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and adjust the sliders under the **Arrangement** submenu to place the selected Patterns more precisely. \- Select all the front pant and pocket Patterns in either the 2D or the 3D Window. Navigate to the Property Editor. Under **Arrangement** , adjust the slider for **Position Y** and move the selected Patterns upward. * **Arranging the Back Pant Patterns YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fT294mK7VZI **\- The back pant Patterns and the yoke Patterns need to be arranged together. \- In the 3D Window, place the back pant Patterns closer to the yoke Patterns. Next, select the back pant Patterns and the yoke Patterns. Click on an Arrangement Point to place the Patterns around the Avatar. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and adjust the sliders under the **Arrangement** submenu to place the selected Patterns more precisely. * **Arranging the Waistband YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nc3NMBTf2E0 **\- Arrange the back waistband Patterns on the back waist Arrangement Points. \- Arrange the front waistband Patterns on the front waist Arrangement Points. \- The right front waistband Pattern must be placed in front of the left front waistband Pattern for stable Simulation. **Sewing the Waistband** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTXoRbwRy7k \- Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024200668/mceclip1.png) **Trace** tool. Select the purple Baseline on the overlap of the waistband and hit the Enter key on the keyboard to generate an Internal Line. \- Copy and Paste the newly created Internal Line to the underlap of the waistband. \- Use the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024200508/mceclip0.png) **Segment Sewing** tool to sew the two Internal Lines together. **Applying Bonding** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hLvWvuiNLkw \- To express interfacing, select the waistband Patterns and use the Bond function. \- Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024190768/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool. In the 2D grid, click on and drag over all of the waistband Patterns. The Patterns must be fully encompassed within the marquee box to be properly selected. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and scroll down to **Bond/Skive**. Click the white arrow to expand the menu and check the checkbox next to **Bond**. The waistband Patterns will change to a deep champagne color in both Windows to indicate that **Bond** has been applied. **Simulation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QvRzKlDOwc8 \- Click on the ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** icon in the 3D Toolbar to apply the changes. Click ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024191328/mceclip6.png) **Simulate** again to turn it off when the 3D Garment is fully draped. **Changing the Avatar Pose** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSyAHNxq6XQ \- Change the Avatar Pose from A-pose to have her stand at attention. \- To apply the Pose, navigate to and double click on the default folder named Pose in the Library. Thumbnails of Avatar faces will appear—double click on the folder that matches the Avatar in the 3D Window. Double click on or drag and drop the file pose_02_attention.pos to apply the pose. Go back to the List of Contents
